Alyssa —

Thanks for sending — received the redlines and the pricing appendix. I took a first pass with Ben and looped Legal (cc'd Laura). A few notes before we escalate to contracts:

- Invoicing entity: Redwood typically invoices our US entity for hosted products; for EU VAT compliance we can either: 1) invoice NovaMed AB directly from Redwood EU subsidiary (needs finance & tax sign-off), or 2) invoice the US entity and treat VAT via reverse charge where applicable. Laura — can you confirm whether Finance can support invoicing from our EU entity for this deal?

- Net terms: Net-45 is not our standard for new commercial customers. Standard is Net-30; for committed reserved capacity deals we can consider Net-45 on a case-by-case basis tied to a purchase order and credit approval. Ben — can you run a quick credit check and confirm if we can make an exception given the ARR and the minimum commit in the appendix?

- Minimum commit: The appendix shows a 12-month minimum at tiered pricing with quarterly true-ups. We should clarify proration for partial first-quarter usage and activation fee timing (invoice now vs invoice on activation). Suggest we add a one-line clause: "Activation fee invoiced with first invoice; minimum commit subject to quarterly true-up."

I will prepare a short summary of requested redlines to send to Legal for a focused redline on: invoicing entity, VAT/responsibility, net terms, activation fee timing, and PO reference.

Next steps: Laura to advise on entity; Ben to confirm credit (cc'd). We'll aim to respond with a clean order form or marked redline within 48 hours.

Thanks,

Jonas / team —

Quick legal/tax read here: we can get this to work but need to lock two items before finalizing the order form.

1) Invoicing entity & VAT: Redwood can invoice from our EU entity, but Finance needs time to validate tax residency and bank routing. If NovaMed requires invoicing from NovaMed AB (SE) perspective, we'll require: (a) the exact legal entity name and VAT ID, (b) confirmation on who bears VAT (customer pays VAT or reverse-charge). If customer will self-account via reverse-charge we need a clause: "Customer shall provide VAT ID and accept reverse-charge where applicable."

2) Net terms + credit: Net-45 is permissible only after procurement provides a PO and our Credit team confirms the credit envelope. Ben: please advise if the credit check can be expedited — if not, propose a staged approach: Net-30 until PO/credit complete, then amend to Net-45 for subsequent invoices.

3) Activation fee & proration: We should add a small fallback language that activation fee is non-refundable and initial quarter will be prorated based on activation date; quarterly true-ups will reconcile actual usage against the minimum commit.

I've proposed editable language below that Legal can drop into the order form redline (feel free to copy to the PDF redline):
- "Invoices shall be issued to the entity specified by Customer. Customer shall provide legal entity name and VAT identification number. Customer is responsible for VAT where applicable unless otherwise agreed in writing. Where reverse-charge applies, Customer shall self-account and provide required declarations."
- "Payment terms: Net-30 by default. Net-45 may be agreed following Credit approval and receipt of an executed purchase order; payment terms prior to Credit approval remain Net-30."
- "Activation fee: invoiced on commencement and non-refundable. Partial quarter usage shall be prorated and reconciled as part of quarterly true-ups against minimum commit."

I will prepare a tracked change PDF and upload to the DocuSign link once Finance confirms the EU invoicing path. Alyssa — if you can share NovaMed AB VAT ID and the PO contact, that will speed things up.
